issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository introduces a different interface name 'Dairy' and has Goat and Seal implement 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. Additionally, there is an empty/unused Milkable.java file in the solution. This name/type mismatch between 'Milkable' and 'Dairy' is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which interface to implement and may break automated tests or comparisons that expect 'Milkable'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename 'Dairy' in the solution to 'Milkable' and ensure it declares String messageOnMilk(), and update Goat and Seal to implement Milkable; or (B) update the problem statement and template to refer to 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. Also remove or implement the empty Milkable.java file in the solution so only the intended interface name remains.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the interface as 'Milkable', but the solution introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (and leaves Milkable.java effectively empty). This is a naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the milk-providing interface) and will confuse students who are asked to implement/use 'Milkable' but see 'Dairy' in the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and update file name to Milkable.java and all implementing classes to implement Milkable), or change all references in the problem/template to 'Dairy'. Preferably keep the problem/template name 'Milkable' and update the solution to provide a proper Milkable interface and remove/merge the Dairy file so students can directly map the requirement to the implementation.
